**Context Note: Kitchen Remodel Project Summary (As of April 7, 2024)**

The kitchen remodel for a 1968 home is underway, with a focus on modern functionality, long-term durability, and minimal maintenance. The project includes a wall move to convert a cramped galley kitchen into an L-shaped layout with a central island, located where the dining room door previously was. This decision was made after testing tape outlines of three options (galley expansion, L-shape with island, U-shape with peninsula) for one week; the L-shape was selected for its superior flow, natural work triangle, and sense of openness.

The final layout is approved and will not be revised. The central island will include a 48-inch base, undermount sink, and built-in seating. No open shelving will be used — closed cabinetry is required for all storage. Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) flooring was tested via samples placed in the hallway for one week; it was rejected due to a plasticky appearance and poor aesthetic in natural light. Vinyl plank is permanently off the table for the main floor.

The countertop will be a quartz composite (not natural marble) due to its resistance to etching, stains, and daily wear. This decision was made after a design review with Naomi, who presented a viable alternative that met aesthetic and practical needs.

The structural beam replacing the wall is an LVL (laminated veneer lumber) measuring 3.5” x 11.875”, per a structural engineer’s letter. This detail is documented and must be referenced in all future construction and inspection phases.

The general contractor is Bogdan Construction. Hartwell Builders were rejected after missing two walkthroughs and submitting a bid that omitted demolition — a critical oversight. Hartwell is permanently off the project.

The project will not use a HELOC or any variable-rate financing. All funding will come from savings and a fixed-rate loan. This policy is non-negotiable.

The term “the sub” refers exclusively to the electrical subcontractor hired by Bogdan — not the subfloor. The subfloor is a separate structural element and was found to have a water stain, which is being addressed separately.

“Cedar” refers only to the back deck rebuild, not the cedar closet lining upstairs. This distinction is strictly enforced in all communications.

The building permit was filed on February 6, 2024, for $342. The review period is 8–10 business days. No action is required until approval is received.

The change order process is formal and documented: any change must be submitted in writing, approved by the homeowner, and signed before work begins. No verbal or informal changes will be accepted.

The budget tracker uses a 3-column system: committed, spent, and remaining. A contingency fund is included, and the team will begin evaluating scope cuts if 50% of the contingency is spent.

The electrical subcontractor (referred to as “the sub”) is confirmed for the week of April 14, 2024. This is critical for downstream work.

The final design template is approved. Lead time from approval to completion is expected to be 4–8 weeks, depending on permitting and scheduling.

The team will not accept any new design options or revisions to the approved layout. Naomi’s design is final.

Open threads: final inspection timing, final finish selections, and final walkthrough logistics.

Next steps: confirm electrical subcontractor availability, begin permitting follow-up, and initiate flooring and cabinetry procurement.

- The kitchen remodel is a full-scale renovation of a 1968 home, including wall removal, layout redesign, and integration of structural, mechanical, and aesthetic upgrades. The project is being managed by a general contractor (Bogdan) and a designer (Naomi), with all communication centralized in this chat for documentation and continuity.

- **Final Layout Decision**: The L-shaped kitchen with a central island (located where the dining room door previously was) has been officially selected. This was determined after testing tape outlines of three options (1) widened galley, (2) L-shape with island, (3) U-shape with peninsula) for one week. The L-shape was chosen for its natural flow, functional work triangle, and sense of spatial balance. The island will include seating and storage.

- **Counter Material**: Real marble was considered but rejected due to maintenance concerns (etching from acids, staining). The chosen alternative is a quartz composite that mimics marble veining but resists stains, heat, and acids. This decision was made to prioritize durability and low maintenance.

- **Flooring**: Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) was tested via samples placed in the hallway for one week. The material appeared plasticky and low-quality under natural light. The partner vetoed it on sight. LVP is permanently off the table for the main kitchen floor.

- **No Open Shelving**: A firm design boundary has been established: no open shelving will be used anywhere in the kitchen. This decision was made to avoid daily dusting, maintenance, and the pressure of "staging" shelves for guests. This is a non-negotiable principle.

- **Financing**: No HELOC, no variable-rate loans, and no revolving credit will be used. All funding will come from savings and a fixed-rate loan. This policy is final and will not be reconsidered.

- **“The Sub”**: Refers exclusively to the electrical subcontractor hired by Bogdan. This is not to be confused with the subfloor. The term “sub” in this context is reserved for the electrician only.

- **“Cedar”**: In this project, “Cedar” refers only to the back deck rebuild. It does not refer to the upstairs cedar closet lining idea. This distinction is strictly enforced to prevent confusion.

- **Permit**: A building permit was filed on February 6, 2024, for $342. The review period is 8–10 business days. No action is required until approval is received.

- **Contingency**: The contingency fund will not be touched until 15% of the total approved budget has been spent. At that point, a formal review will occur to assess and potentially reduce non-essential scope.

- **Change Orders**: All changes must be documented via a formal change order. The process includes proposal, written approval, cost and timeline impact, and signature. No verbal or informal changes will be accepted.

- **Subcontractor Confirmation**: The electrical subcontractor (the "sub") is confirmed for the week of April 14, 2024. This is critical for timing downstream work.

- **Deck Work**: The back deck rebuild (referred to as "Cedar") will not begin until after the framing inspection clears. It cannot run in parallel.

- **Open Threads**: Final confirmation of the electrical subcontractor’s schedule (week of April 14), final approval of the design template, and tracking of the 15% contingency trigger.

- **Ruled Out**: LVP flooring, open shelving, HELOC financing, and any use of "Cedar" to refer to the closet. The U-shape and galley layouts were tested and rejected in favor of the L-shape.

- **Next Steps**: Finalize design template, confirm subcontractor availability, begin permit review tracking, and initiate weekly check-ins with Bogdan using the 5-part progress template.
